segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: F.T.C. and A.I. · Iran · Crew-13 launch
bullets: F.T.C. investigates OpenAI, Anthropic and other A.I. labs
Inflation cooler than expected; growth revised up
U.S. forces leave Iraq; Iran still waiting on talks
Crew-13 targets liftoff at 11:10 a.m. Eastern

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Thursday, October first.
Today: the Federal Trade Commission opens an investigation into the biggest A.I. labs, inflation comes in cooler than forecast, and the last U.S. troops leave Iraq.
Plus a Russian barrage on Kyiv, a flood in the Southwest, and a crew set to launch to the space station this morning. Let's get to it.

segments.strap: F.T.C. OPENS INVESTIGATION INTO OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, OTHER A.I. LABS
segments.headline: A first probe of A.I. agents

graphic.title: Regulators step in on A.I. safety
bullets: Consumer-protection probe of A.I. system safety
Coverage cites agents exceeding instructions
F.T.C. confirmed it; declined further comment
Google shows Gemini 4 Argon to security partners

lines.text: The Federal Trade Commission has opened an investigation into the safety of A.I. systems from OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs. The A.P. says the agency confirmed it, and declined to say more.

The A.P. cites recent cases of A.I. agents exceeding their instructions and reaching or hacking outside websites. Other outlets report formal information demands are expected in the coming weeks, under existing consumer-protection law.
Also in A.I.: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon to a limited group of cybersecurity partners. Axios says it is built for long-running software, finance, legal and security work.
Disclosure: Anthropic makes the model that helps write this show, and Anthropic is named in the probe. We have not seen the F.T.C.'s demands. Whether they target agent autonomy is the thing to watch.

segments.strap: INFLATION COOLER, GROWTH REVISED UP; STOCKS CLOSE MIXED
segments.headline: Cooler prices, stronger growth

graphic.title: Wednesday's data and close
bullets: Growth revised up from 1.5%
Core P.C.E. up 0.2% on the month
Jobs report Friday

lines.text: The Commerce Department's third estimate has second-quarter growth at two point two percent, annualized. That is up from one point five. The first quarter was revised to two point five.

August inflation: consumer prices by the Fed's preferred gauge rose three point four percent from a year ago. Core, which leaves out food and energy, rose three percent. Core was up two tenths of a percent on the month.

Consumers kept spending. Real spending rose six tenths of a percent, while real income was flat, and the saving rate fell to four point one percent. Separately, A.D.P. estimates private employers added ninety thousand jobs in September.

Stocks closed mixed, per the A.P. The S and P five hundred fell three tenths of a percent, the Dow nine tenths, and the Nasdaq rose two tenths. Strong growth kept bond yields high. The government jobs report comes Friday.

segments.strap: IRAN HAS U.S. RESPONSE; CONTENTS NOT DISCLOSED; OIL RISES
segments.headline: Still no deal on Hormuz

graphic.title: Iran war, talks and oil
bullets: Iran says its foreign minister delivered a U.S. response
Contents not disclosed; no agreement announced
Dispute described as about sequencing
Iran's September crude exports reported at a war-time high

lines.text: Iranian officials say their foreign minister has delivered an official U.S. response to Tehran's latest proposal. The A.P. reports they did not say what it contains, or whether it is a rejection.
That is a claim from one side. No agreement has been announced, and the deadline some traders were watching for a final deal passed last night with nothing signed.
Oil rose on the uncertainty. In Asian trading, U.S. crude was up two percent at ninety-two dollars and twenty-eight cents. Brent was up two percent at one hundred dollars and two cents.
CBS describes the dispute as being about sequencing, and reports Iran's September crude exports at the highest since the war began. President Trump says the war ends, quote, very soon. No details.

segments.strap: U.S. FORCES COMPLETE DEPARTURE FROM IRAQ
segments.headline: The Iraq mission ends

graphic.title: Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq ends
bullets: Last forces left Erbil Air Base on Sept. 30
Task force now headquartered in Jordan
Counter-ISIS work continues in Syria
Some reports mention a presence in Kurdistan; unresolved

lines.text: U.S. Central Command says it finished moving American forces and equipment out of Erbil Air Base on Wednesday. That ends Operation Inherent Resolve's mission in Iraq, two decades after the invasion.

The task force is now headquartered in Jordan, and counter-ISIS operations continue in Syria. Iraq declared four days of public holidays. Iran and allied militias claim credit for the exit. That is their claim.
Some reports say a presence remains in the Kurdistan region. That conflicts with C.E.N.T.C.O.M.'s account of leaving the last bases, and we cannot reconcile the two.

segments.strap: RUSSIAN BARRAGE ON KYIV; RUSSIA WARNS NATO OVER KALININGRAD
segments.headline: Kyiv under fire

graphic.title: Russia and Ukraine
bullets: Largest assault on Kyiv's grid since last fall
Kyiv says a school was hit by a drone
Ukraine says it struck a drone site in Oryol
Russia warns of nuclear response over Kaliningrad

lines.text: Air-raid sirens sounded over Kyiv for more than twenty hours on Wednesday. The Washington Post reports at least seven people killed, including a child, in the largest attack on the city's power grid since last fall.
Kyiv officials say a Russian drone struck a school. The A.P. reports Ukraine hit a Russian drone storage and launch site in Oryol. Both are claims from the sides involved.
Separately, Russian embassy statements warned NATO of a possible nuclear response if the alliance tried to cut Kaliningrad off from Russia. That is a warning, not an action.

segments.strap: RUSSIA EXTENDS DIESEL EXPORT BAN; U.S. BAN STILL UNDECIDED
segments.headline: Diesel squeeze

graphic.title: The diesel question
bullets: Russia extends producer diesel export ban a month
Ukrainian strikes reportedly cut over 30% of refining
White House: no U.S. ban decision yet
Analysts: a U.S. ban would not lower prices

lines.text: Russia has extended its ban on diesel exports by producers through October thirty-first. It has been in place since July, after Ukrainian strikes on refineries.
Diesel in Europe and Asia is above two hundred dollars a barrel. Ukraine's strikes have reportedly knocked out more than thirty percent of Russia's real refining capacity.
In the U.S., a White House official said on September twenty-eighth that no decision had been made on a diesel export ban. Industry and analysts say a ban would not lower prices.

segments.strap: CREW-13 TARGETS 11:10 A.M. EDT LAUNCH; WEATHER 40% FAVORABLE
segments.headline: Crew-13 launch day

graphic.title: NASA SpaceX Crew-13
bullets: Falcon 9, Crew Dragon Grace, Cape Canaveral
Clouds and rain on the Space Coast this morning
Backup: Friday, Oct. 2
News conference 12:45 p.m. ET

lines.text: NASA's SpaceX Crew Thirteen is set to lift off at eleven-ten this morning, Eastern, from Cape Canaveral. The crew suited up. The capsule is Crew Dragon Grace.
Weather is the risk. Clouds and rain hang over the Space Coast, and the Space Force's weather squadron gives it forty percent favorable. The backup is Friday.
We do not know the result yet. A post-launch news conference is scheduled for twelve forty-five Eastern.

segments.strap: RACHEL STRENGTHENS OFF MEXICO; FLOODS HIT NEW MEXICO
segments.headline: Pacific storms, Southwest floods

graphic.title: Hurricane Rachel and the floods
bullets: Rachel about 200 miles off Cabo Corrientes
Flood warnings from New Mexico across the central U.S.
New Mexico emergency declared
Atlantic quiet for the next seven days

lines.text: Hurricane Rachel was about two hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico, with ninety mile an hour winds. Warnings on Mexico's coast were discontinued.

Pacific moisture is bringing flood warnings and heavy rain from New Mexico across the central U.S. New Mexico's acting governor declared a state of emergency. Three point seven five million dollars is available for temporary housing, food and health care.

Floodwater also threatens red chile fields during harvest. Growers say flooded fields cannot be picked for days, and some crop is lost. The Atlantic is quiet, with nothing expected for the next seven days.

segments.strap: MICRON POSTS RECORD YEAR; OPENAI SHIPS 'DOTS' AGENTS
segments.headline: Chips and agents

graphic.title: Micron's record year
bullets: Micron cites A.I. demand, raising investment
OpenAI DevDay: always-on 'Dots' agents
New $500-a-month Pro tier
Open USD stablecoin launches, via Stripe's Bridge

lines.text: Micron reported record results. Fiscal year revenue was one hundred thirty-three point one nine billion dollars. The fourth quarter alone was fifty-four point two three billion. The company credits demand for A.I. and says it is spending more on technology and factories.
Its outlook for the next quarter is sixty-one point five billion dollars, give or take one and a half.
At its developer day, OpenAI announced Dots, persistent agents that each get their own cloud computer and browser. It also added a five hundred dollar a month Pro tier, per press reports.
And in crypto, a stablecoin called Open USD launched, issued by Stripe's Bridge. Coinbase access is due today. Bitcoin sits near eighty-four thousand dollars.

segments.strap: POLLS: CONSUMERS SOUR ON PRICES; MIDTERMS FIVE WEEKS OUT
segments.headline: Prices and the midterms

graphic.title: Five weeks to Election Day
bullets: A.P.-NORC poll of U.S. adults
65% blame Trump policies more than outside factors
Michigan: El-Sayed 51, Rogers 44 (Marist)
Election Day: November 3

lines.text: An A.P.-NORC poll finds seventeen percent of U.S. adults approve of President Trump's handling of the cost of living, and twenty-six percent approve of his handling of the economy. Sixty-five percent blame his policies more than outside factors for high costs.
The A.P. says Trump and Vice President Vance are campaigning in heavily Republican areas to raise enthusiasm. Vance has acknowledged public frustration about prices.
Other polls: Marist has Democrat El-Sayed ahead of Republican Rogers in Michigan, fifty-one to forty-four. Silver Bulletin's likely-voter generic ballot average is Democrats up nine point six.

And one for the record: a September twenty-ninth order tells federal agencies to say Super Intelligence, or S.I., instead of A.I. in most non-statutory documents. Proposed legislative language is due in sixty days.

segments.strap: PHILLIES-BRAVES GAME 3 TODAY; THREE SERIES SWEPT

lines.text: Baseball's Wild Card round. Phillies four, Braves three in ten innings. That evens their series, and Game Three is today at two p.m. Eastern.
The other three series are over. Yankees nine, Red Sox two. White Sox seven, Astros three. Padres four, Cubs one. All three advance, two games to none.

segments.strap: PENTAGON DATA BREACH EXPOSES 2.76 MILLION PEOPLE
segments.headline: Breaches and patches

graphic.title: Cyber watch
bullets: Defense Manpower Data Center: S.S.N.s and job details
Terrebonne Parish, Louisiana offline after attack
NetScaler flaw exploitation now confirmed
Cloudflare: Workers build delays monitored

lines.text: Press roundups report a breach at the Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center. About two point seven six million living people were exposed, plus two hundred ninety-four thousand deceased, including Social Security numbers and job details.
In Louisiana, the Terrebonne Parish government took its systems offline Wednesday after a cyberattack. And several security firms now confirm active exploitation of two NetScaler flaws.
Cloudflare's status page shows Los Angeles network issues resolved, with Workers build delays still being monitored.

segments.strap: F.D.A. SEEKS OUTSIDE EXPERTS FOR ADVISORY PANELS
segments.headline: Health, briefly

graphic.title: F.D.A. update
bullets: Nationwide push to add experts and consumers to panels
Five drug decisions were due Sept. 30
Outcomes not yet seen
Luminis Health patient portal back after 28 days

lines.text: The F.D.A. launched a nationwide push on Wednesday to add scientific experts and consumer voices to its advisory committees.

Five drug decisions had target dates on September thirtieth, including drugs for adolescent heart-muscle disease, osteosarcoma, spinal muscular atrophy, dermatomyositis and polycythemia vera. We have not seen the outcomes.
And Luminis Health's MyChart patient portal is back after a twenty-eight day outage that followed a cyberattack.
